title: Carbon management revives CCS in Germany as safeguards steadily weaken
excerpt: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) is regaining prominence in climate policy debates in Germany. content_html:
Carbon capture and storage (CCS) is regaining prominence in climate policy debates in Germany. A study published in Environmental Politics examines the reasons behind this comeback and shows that the strict limits originally envisaged for CCS were progressively relaxed throughout the political process. This increases the risk that the lifespan of fossil fuel infrastructure will be prolonged, potentially sidelining other climate protection measures.

"In Germany, CCS was long regarded as a political non-starter. This makes the question of how the technology returned to the center of the climate policy debate within just a few years all the more intriguing," says lead author Tobias Haas from the Research Institute for Sustainability at the GFZ (RIFS). In the late 2000s, an initial attempt to introduce CCS failed due to resistance from local initiatives, environmental NGOs and low public acceptance. The technology subsequently fell out of political favor for years, although it continued to be viewed as a critical element in climate scenarios for achieving neutrality.

New narrative fosters greater acceptance

The political comeback was initiated by the so-called "traffic light" coalition government (2021–2024), which revised the Carbon Dioxide Storage Act, developed a carbon management strategy and worked on a long-term strategy for unavoidable residual emissions. The establishment of the umbrella term "carbon management" opened the door to many technological approaches. In addition to CCS, these include the use of captured carbon dioxide (Carbon Capture and Utilization, CCU) as well as processes for removing CO₂ from the atmosphere (Carbon Dioxide Removal, CDR).

"The concept of carbon management is politically appealing because it places CCS in a new context," explains Haas. "The technology is no longer discussed in isolation as a controversial process, but as part of a more comprehensive management approach." This shift in perspective played a key role in the political resurgence of CCS.

How rather than whether

At the same time, the debate shifted: The argument was no longer about whether CCS should be used; instead, the focus turned to how and to what extent its use should be permitted. In the process, the conditions originally laid down for the use of the technology were gradually relaxed. At the outset of the debate, there was still broad agreement that CCS should only be used where CO₂ emissions could not be avoided for technical reasons and that avoiding emissions must, in principle, take precedence.

In 2025, the current federal government passed an amendment to the Carbon Dioxide Storage Act.

While this continues to place the emphasis on storage beneath the seabed, the original restrictions on its use were further relaxed. The law only excludes coal-fired power plants from using CCS—plants that are already scheduled for decommissioning by 2038. At the same time, the federal government is planning additional power plant capacity of 12 gigawatts, which is to become climate-neutral by 2045 using "technology-neutral" approaches. In the authors' view, this could also facilitate the use of CCS in new gas-fired power plants and thus prolong dependency on fossil fuels.

A clear definition of "hard-to-abate emissions" is needed

The study identifies three reasons why the originally envisaged strict limits on the use of CCS could not be enforced: Environmental organizations held differing positions, which weakened their collective political clout. At the same time, the public debate increasingly lost sight of the fact that many supporters were only willing to allow CCS under strict conditions. Finally, the conditions were further watered down during a protracted political decision-making process.

The authors therefore recommend that the use of CCS be contingent upon clearly defined conditions. Central to this is a binding definition of which emissions are truly "hard-to-abate." "Otherwise, there is a risk that more and more emissions will subsequently be classified as unavoidable and that the use of CCS will be gradually expanded," says Haas. The role of CCS is therefore not merely a technical or economic matter, but a political decision regarding the path Germany wishes to take toward climate neutrality. The debate surrounding CCS exemplifies the risk of relying, in order to achieve climate targets, on technologies that have yet to make a tangible contribution to climate protection and where it is unclear whether they will "deliver" on a large scale in the future.

More information

Tobias Haas et al, The renaissance of carbon capture and storage in Germany and the politics of conditionality, Environmental Politics (2026). DOI: 10.1080/09644016.2026.2700726

碳捕获与封存（CCS）在德国气候政策辩论中重新占据重要地位。 发表在《环境政治》上的一项研究探讨了这种卷土重来背后的原因，并表明最初设想的对 CCS 的严格限制在整个政治进程中逐渐放松。 这增加了化石燃料基础设施寿命延长的风险，可能导致其他气候保护措施被搁置。

“在德国，CCS 长期以来一直被认为在政治上是不可能成功的。 这使得该技术如何在短短几年内重新回到气候政策辩论中心的问题变得更加有趣，”来自 GFZ 可持续发展研究所 (RIFS) 的主要作者托比亚斯·哈斯 (Tobias Haas) 说道。 2000 年代末，由于当地倡议、环保非政府组织的抵制以及公众接受度较低，引入 CCS 的初步尝试失败了。 尽管该技术仍然被视为实现中立的气候情景中的关键要素，但该技术随后多年来不再受到政治青睐。

新的叙述促进了更多的接受

这次政治卷土重来是由所谓的“红绿灯”联合政府（2021-2024年）发起的，该政府修订了《二氧化碳封存法》，制定了碳管理战略，并制定了针对不可避免的残余排放的长期战略。 “碳管理”这一总称的建立为许多技术方法打开了大门。 除了 CCS 之外，这些措施还包括使用捕获的二氧化碳（碳捕获和利用，CCU）以及从大气中去除二氧化碳的工艺（二氧化碳去除，CDR）。

“碳管理的概念在政治上很有吸引力，因为它将 CCS 置于新的背景下，”哈斯解释道。 “该技术不再作为一个有争议的过程而被孤立地讨论，而是作为更全面的管理方法的一部分。” 这种观点的转变在 CCS 的政治复兴中发挥了关键作用。

如何而不是是否

与此同时，争论发生了转变：争论不再是关于是否应该使用CCS；而是关于是否应该使用CCS。相反，焦点转向如何以及在何种程度上应允许其使用。 在此过程中，最初规定的使用该技术的条件逐渐放宽。 辩论一开始，人们仍然普遍认为，CCS 只能在由于技术原因无法避免二氧化碳排放的情况下使用，并且原则上必须优先考虑避免排放。

2025年，现任联邦政府通过了《二氧化碳封存法》修正案。

虽然这仍然强调海底储存，但最初对其使用的限制进一步放宽。 该法律仅排除燃煤电厂使用 CCS，即已计划于 2038 年退役的电厂。 与此同时，联邦政府正计划增加 12 吉瓦的发电厂容量，以采用“技术中立”方法，到 2045 年实现气候中和。 作者认为，这还可以促进 CCS 在新燃气发电厂中的使用，从而延长对化石燃料的依赖。

需要对“难以减排”做出明确定义

该研究指出了最初设想的对CCS使用的严格限制无法执行的三个原因： 环保组织持有不同的立场，这削弱了它们的集体政治影响力。 与此同时，公众辩论越来越忽视了一个事实，即许多支持者只愿意在严格的条件下允许CCS。 最后，在漫长的政治决策过程中，这些条件被进一步淡化。

因此，作者建议 CCS 的使用取决于明确定义的条件。 其核心是对哪些排放真正“难以减少”做出具有约束力的定义。 “否则，存在的风险是越来越多的排放随后将被归类为不可避免的，并且 CCS 的使用将逐渐扩大，”哈斯说。 因此，CCS 的作用不仅仅是技术或经济问题，而且是关于德国希望走向气候中和的道路的政治决定。 围绕 CCS 的争论体现了为实现气候目标而依赖尚未对气候保护做出切实贡献且尚不清楚这些技术未来是否会大规模“交付”的技术的风险。
